reason: The user explicitly rejected synchronized reflection sway and reported a regression at the horizon. Local distortion replaces only that obsolete motion expectation; the three-pixel contact fade was a demonstrated source of the visible horizon rule. The old ceiling-buffer assertion was explicitly replaced because its partial-alpha terminal row contributes a seam at fractional pixel density; only whole opaque source rows are now sampled.
previousBehavior: The entire reflected scene used one affine shear, and opacity fell linearly within three pixels of the waterline.
intendedBehavior: Reflected patches distort independently with continuous pixel sampling. Horizon contact starts with a flat opacity slope and fades gradually without a straight rule.
replacementTests: RISK landscape water: reflection distortion varies across the lake without rigid sway
RISK landscape water browser: GPU distortion preserves contact and sharp pixels while patches move independently
RISK landscape water: lake clip overlaps the horizon contact at fractional pixel densities
RISK regression gate: changing existing tests requires a specific reason and replacement coverage
RISK regression gate: insertions cannot silently disable existing assertions
preservedCoverage: Natural reflected height, full-resolution sampling, local motion boundedness and smooth 30fps steps.
Stationary horizon contact, eased opacity, no overlay contours, restrained original glints and reduced motion.
Existing floating-object reflection, celestial timing and lighting, train tracks, electrical and vehicle layering tests remain intact.

redEvidence.command: node --test --test-name-pattern='reflection distortion varies|lake clip overlaps|reflection opacity meets' tests.js (run separately before each implementation)
redEvidence.failure: Before implementation, the tests failed on whole-image motion.shear, missing fractional lakeContact overlap, and contactDepth outside 12-18 pixels. Regression gate test also first failed because validateRegressionChanges was undefined. Full-suite validation also caught the old ceiling-buffer contract; its updated assertion now preserves the full-size mirror while requiring an opaque edge. Add-only return and moved-insertion gate fixtures each failed before their corresponding guard fixes. Appended executable-code exemption was removed after red fixtures showed new test additions and process termination could evade explanation.
